notes.2: Full marks were common on this question, but some candidates did not know pommes de terre in 2(a) or poires in 2(d) .
notes.3: Candidates performed well on this question, but some did not know banlieue de Paris and sœur jumelle to answer 3(a) and 3(b) .
notes.4: For this exercise, candidates were required to read a more extended text in which Caroline wrote about Christmas with her family. The text was mostly straightforward, and the vocabulary covered familiar topics. Overall, candidates performed well on this exercise. The text was written in the first person, and the questions used the third person. Most questions could be answered by lifting a small number of words from the text, but the answers to Questions 4(c) and 4(f) required a minor manipulation to gain the mark. If candidates chose to lift more than was required to answer the other questions, they had to make any manipulation needed in the extra material, usually involving going from the first to the third person. It is generally advised to answer with the minimum number of words. In 4(a) , some candidates did not understand the question word comment. For 4(d) , some candidates misread the question and answered il pleuvait . For 4(f) , some candidates changed the verb from avoir to être and some answered in the present tense. Some candidates omitted the important preposition sous to answer 4(g) . For 4(i) , some candidates answered with une longue promenade which did not answer the question où? For 4(j) , some candidates omitted de mer in their answer and could not gain the mark, others invalidated their answer by adding les salades .
notes.5: In this exercise, candidates had to match a series of descriptions with statements from five people looking for a leisure centre. This exercise is aimed at the higher grades and the texts need to be read more closely in order to find the option that suits best. Each person’s statement gave quite specific requirements for the sort of leisure centre that they were looking for, and these details excluded all answers except the correct one. The statements included factors such as swimming pool, fitness classes or tennis courts. Candidates need to ensure they consider all the information given as this is not a gist comprehension question Description 1 was a frequent incorrect answer for 5(a) .
notes.6: This final exercise about pocket money was intended to be the most challenging part of the paper. About half the questions can be answered with a careful lift from the text and the others need a small manipulation of the text to answer the question. Very few candidates achieved full marks, and the questions seem to have discriminated appropriately. Although verbs do not necessarily have to be correct to score a mark, the tense usually must be appropriate to the question. Some candidates chose to paraphrase the text rather than lift words from the text. There is no need to do this, and although some candidates did this well, others used inappropriate synonyms when paraphrasing and could not gain the mark. In 6(a) , some candidates invalidated their answer by adding étant donné que. In 6(c) , candidates did not always link la plupart in the question to principalement in the text. In questions requiring a manipulation of the text, candidates often answered in the first person.
